subject: maths
title: Angles: Missing Angles in Triangles, Quadrilaterals and Regular Polygons
seo_title: Year 6 Angles Worksheets: Missing Angles, Vertically Opposite, Triangles and Regular Polygons (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Find unknown angles in any triangles, quadrilaterals, and regular polygons; recognise angles where they meet at a point, are on a straight line, or are vertically opposite, and find missing angles.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on angles: angles on a straight line and around a point, vertically opposite angles, missing angles in triangles and quadrilaterals, and angles in regular polygons, plus SATs-style problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Straight line 180°, around a point 360°, triangle 180°, quadrilateral 360°, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
key_sub: Add the angles you know and subtract from the right total. In a regular polygon each exterior angle is 360° ÷ number of sides, and the angle inside is 180° minus that.
body_html:
Five angle facts

To find a missing angle, find the fact that fits the picture. Then add the angles you know and subtract from the total.

Where the angles areAngle fact
On a straight lineThey add up to 180°
Around a pointThey add up to 360°
Vertically opposite (two lines cross)They are equal
Inside a triangleThey add up to 180°
Inside a quadrilateralThey add up to 360°
Example

Two angles on a straight line are 47° and ?. Find ?.

Straight line, so 180°. 180° − 47° = 133°. Check: 47° + 133° = 180°.

Answer: 133°

Triangles and quadrilaterals

The angles inside a triangle add up to 180°. A quadrilateral splits into 2 triangles, so its angles add up to 360°. In an isosceles triangle, the two base angles are equal. Marks on the sides show which two sides are equal.

Isosceles triangle

The angle at the top of an isosceles triangle is 40°. Find each base angle.

180° − 40° = 140°. The two base angles are equal: 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.

Answer: 70° each

Regular polygons

A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles. Walk around it: you turn through the exterior angles, and they add up to 360°. So each exterior angle is 360° ÷ number of sides. The angle inside is 180° minus that.

Regular polygonExterior angleAngle inside
Equilateral triangle (3 sides)360° ÷ 3 = 120°60°
Square (4 sides)360° ÷ 4 = 90°90°
Pentagon (5 sides)360° ÷ 5 = 72°108°
Hexagon (6 sides)360° ÷ 6 = 60°120°
Octagon (8 sides)360° ÷ 8 = 45°135°
Regular pentagon

Find each angle inside a regular pentagon.

Triangles: 3 × 180° = 540°, and 540° ÷ 5 = 108°. Or exterior angles: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°, and 180° − 72° = 108°.

Answer: 108°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 360° for a straight line, or 180° around a pointStraight line: 180°. All the way round: 360°
Using 180° for a quadrilateralA quadrilateral is 2 triangles: 360°
Thinking vertically opposite angles add up to 180°Opposite angles are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°
Not halving for the two equal angles of an isosceles triangleSubtract the top angle from 180°, then divide by 2
Giving 360° ÷ n as the angle inside a regular polygon360° ÷ n is the exterior angle. Inside: 180° minus it
Measuring a diagram marked “not drawn accurately”Calculate with angle facts. Do not measure

faq.q: What angle facts do Year 6 pupils need to know?
faq.a: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, angles around a point add up to 360°, vertically opposite angles are equal, angles in a triangle add up to 180° and angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°.

faq.q: How do you find a missing angle in a triangle?
faq.a: Add the two angles you know and subtract the total from 180°. In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal, so you may need to halve.

faq.q: How do you work out the angles inside a regular polygon?
faq.a: Divide 360° by the number of sides to get the exterior angle, then subtract it from 180°. For a regular pentagon: 360° ÷ 5 = 72°, so each angle inside is 108°.

faq.q: Are missing-angle questions in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes, angle questions often appear in the reasoning papers (Papers 2 and 3). Diagrams are usually marked “not drawn accurately”, so pupils must calculate with angle facts, not measure.

sets.title: Angles on a straight line and around a point

items.e: The line is tilted, but it is still straight: 180° − 142° = 38°.

items.q: Angles around a point add up to …
items.e: Angles around a point make a full turn: 360°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: The whole angle is a right angle. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: A right angle is 90°. 90° − 62° = 28°. (180° − 62° = 118° would be for a straight line.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: First add the angles you know: 45° + 70° = 115°. Then 180° − 115° = 65°.
Angles around a point add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (180° ÷ 3 = 60° would be a straight line.)

items.q: The two angles marked a are equal. What is a?
items.e: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°, and the two equal angles share it: 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.
140° + 135° = 275°. Angles around a point add up to 360°: 360° − 275° = 85°.
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 115° = 65°. (360° − 115° = 245° would be for angles around a point.)

items.q: Three equal angles together make a straight line. How big is each angle?
items.e: The three angles add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. (120° would come from using 360°.)

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle: 90°. 90° + 35° = 125°, and 180° − 125° = 55°.

items.q: Five equal angles fit exactly around a point. How big is each angle?
items.e: Around a point: 360°. 360° ÷ 5 = 72°. (36° comes from 180° ÷ 5.)
Angles around a point add up to 360°. 110° + 135° = 245°, and 360° − 245° = 115°.

items.q: Angles on a straight line add up to …
items.e: A straight line is a half turn: 180°. Two right angles make a straight line.

items.q: Four angles are around a point. One is a right angle and the other three are equal. How big is each of the three equal angles?
items.e: 360° − 90° = 270°. The three equal angles share it: 270° ÷ 3 = 90°.

items.q: The angles are on a straight line. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: 28° + 97° = 125°. Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so 180° − 125° = 55°.
The angles are on a straight line, so they add up to 180°, not 360°. 180° − 130° = 50°.

items.q: Two angles are next to each other. One is 125° and the other is 65°. Can they make a straight line?
items.e: 125° + 65° = 190°. Angles on a straight line must add up to exactly 180°, so they cannot.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 65° angle, so they are equal: 65°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 40° angle, so they are equal: 40°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What do all four angles add up to?
items.e: The four angles go all the way around the crossing point, so they add up to 360°.

items.q: What is true about vertically opposite angles?
items.e: When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are equal. Angles next to each other add up to 180°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Two vertically opposite angles add up to 100°. How big is each of the other two angles?
items.e: The two equal opposite angles are 100° ÷ 2 = 50° each. The angles next to them are 180° − 50° = 130°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: 35° + 85° + the angle above them make a straight line: 180° − 120° = 60°. The missing angle is vertically opposite that angle, so it is 60° too.
The missing angle is vertically opposite the 145° angle, so they are equal: 145°.
Vertically opposite angles are across the crossing point from each other: a and c (also b and d). Angles next to each other, like a and b, add up to 180°.
The missing angle and 146° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 146° = 34°.
a is on a straight line with 64°: 180° − 64° = 116°. b is vertically opposite 64°, so it is 64°. c is vertically opposite a, so it is 116°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The three angles are on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.
The missing angle and 75° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 75° = 105°.
The missing angle and 130° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 130° = 50°.
The missing angle and 58° are next to each other on a straight line, so they add up to 180°. 180° − 58° = 122°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 72° angle, so they are equal: 72°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. One of the angles is a right angle. What are the other three angles?
items.e: The angle next to 90° is 180° − 90° = 90°, and the opposite angles are equal. So all four angles are 90°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. What is the value of y?
items.e: 2y is vertically opposite 80°, so 2y = 80°. Then y = 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

items.q: Freya says that vertically opposite angles add up to 180°. Is she right?
c: Yes, they are on a straight line
items.e: Vertically opposite angles are equal. It is the angles next to each other (on a straight line) that add up to 180°.

items.q: Three straight lines meet at a point. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The missing angle is vertically opposite the 80° angle, so it is also 80°.
p and 105° are on a straight line: 180° − 105° = 75°. q is vertically opposite 105°, so 105°. r is vertically opposite p: 75°.

items.q: An isosceles triangle has one angle of 100°. What are the other two angles?
items.e: 100° is obtuse, so it must be the angle between the equal sides (two angles of 100° would be more than 180°). 180° − 100° = 80°, and 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 50° + 60° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 35° + 105° = 140°, and 180° − 140° = 40°.

items.q: The two angles with a dash are equal. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: Both marked angles are 48°. 48° + 48° = 96°, and 180° − 96° = 84°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 37° and 98°. What is the third angle?
This right-angled triangle is isosceles. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The other two angles share 180° − 90° = 90°. They are equal, so each is 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal. 180° − 40° = 140°, and 140° ÷ 2 = 70°.

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal, so both are 67°. 67° + 67° = 134°, and 180° − 134° = 46°.

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal, so both are 52°. 52° + 52° = 104°, and 180° − 104° = 76°.
The angles in a triangle add up to 180°, not 360°. 65° + 45° = 110°, and 180° − 110° = 70°.
The angle inside the triangle at that corner is 180° − 55° − 70° = 55°. It is on a straight line with ?, so ? = 180° − 55° = 125°.

items.q: A triangle has a right angle and an angle of 45°. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: The third angle is 180° − 90° − 45° = 45°. Two equal angles mean two equal sides, so it is right-angled and isosceles.

items.q: Work out the missing angle in this triangle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle (90°). 90° + 38° = 128°, and 180° − 128° = 52°. (Or: the other two angles add up to 90°, so 90° − 38° = 52°.)

items.q: This is an isosceles triangle. The marks show the two equal sides. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The two base angles are equal. 180° − 110° = 70°, and 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

items.q: Each angle of an equilateral triangle is …
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal angles that add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 24° + 118° = 142°, and 180° − 142° = 38°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 28° + 64° = 92°, and 180° − 92° = 88°.

items.q: Which three angles could be the angles of a triangle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°. 50° + 60° + 70° = 180°. The others add up to 190°, 200° and 360°.
Angles in a triangle add up to 180°. 63° + 45° = 108°, and 180° − 108° = 72°.

items.q: Work out the missing angle in this triangle.
items.e: The small square is a right angle (90°). 90° + 61° = 151°, and 180° − 151° = 29°. (Or: the other two angles add up to 90°, so 90° − 61° = 29°.)

sets.title: Angles in quadrilaterals and regular polygons

items.q: What is the size of each angle inside a regular decagon (10 sides)?
items.e: Each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 10 = 36°. Each angle inside is 180° − 36° = 144°.
Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 70° + 60° + 120° = 250°, and 360° − 250° = 110°.

items.q: This is a regular pentagon. What is the size of each angle inside it?
items.e: A pentagon makes 3 triangles from one corner: 3 × 180° = 540°. 540° ÷ 5 = 108°. (360° ÷ 5 = 72° is the exterior angle, not the angle inside.)

items.q: The angles inside any quadrilateral add up to …
items.e: A quadrilateral can be cut into 2 triangles from one corner: 2 × 180° = 360°.

items.q: Which regular polygon has angles of 90° inside it?
items.e: A square has 4 right angles. An equilateral triangle has 60°, a regular pentagon 108° and a regular hexagon 120°.
Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 80° + 115° + 70° = 265°, and 360° − 265° = 95°.
The two small squares are 90° each. 90° + 90° + 65° = 245°, and 360° − 245° = 115°. (Using 180° instead of 360° gives an impossible answer.)

items.q: This is a regular hexagon. What is the size of each angle inside it?
items.e: A hexagon makes 4 triangles from one corner: 4 × 180° = 720°. 720° ÷ 6 = 120°. (360° ÷ 6 = 60° is the exterior angle.)

items.q: The pentagon is split into triangles from one corner. What do the angles inside a pentagon add up to?
items.e: There are 3 triangles, and each has angles adding up to 180°. 3 × 180° = 540°. (5 × 180° = 900° counts 5 triangles, but there are only 3.)

items.q: What is the size of each angle inside a regular octagon?
items.e: Each exterior angle is 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. Each angle inside is 180° − 45° = 135°. (Or 1,080° ÷ 8 = 135°.)

items.q: What do the angles inside an octagon add up to?
items.e: From one corner an octagon splits into 8 − 2 = 6 triangles. 6 × 180° = 1,080°.

items.q: What do the angles inside a hexagon add up to?
items.e: From one corner a hexagon splits into 6 − 2 = 4 triangles. 4 × 180° = 720°.

items.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 75° and 105°. What is the fourth angle?
Harry says each angle inside a regular hexagon is 60°, because 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. Is he right?
items.e: 360° ÷ 6 = 60° is the exterior angle. The angle inside is 180° − 60° = 120°.

items.q: This is a kite. Its two side angles are equal. Work out the missing angle.
This is a parallelogram. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: In a parallelogram, angles next to each other add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°. Check: 70° + 110° + 70° + 110° = 360°.

items.q: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 45°. How many sides does it have?
items.e: The exterior angles add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 45° = 8, so it has 8 sides (an octagon).

items.q: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular pentagon?
items.e: The exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360°. 360° ÷ 5 = 72°. (108° is the angle inside.)

items.q: Lines are drawn from one corner of a hexagon to the other corners. How many triangles are made?
items.e: From one corner you can draw lines to 3 other corners (not to itself or its 2 neighbours). They make 6 − 2 = 4 triangles.
Angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°. 100° + 120° + 75° = 295°, and 360° − 295° = 65°.

items.q: This is a regular pentagon with one diagonal. Each angle inside the pentagon is 108°. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The diagonal makes an isosceles triangle with two sides of the pentagon. 180° − 108° = 72°, and the two equal angles are 72° ÷ 2 = 36°.

items.q: The triangle is isosceles. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The base angle inside is 180° − 112° = 68°. Both base angles are 68°: 68° + 68° = 136°, and 180° − 136° = 44°.

items.q: The two angles marked x are equal. What is x?
items.e: 180° − 50° = 130°. The two equal angles share it: 130° ÷ 2 = 65°.

items.q: Alfie cuts a round pizza into 8 equal slices from the centre. What angle does each slice make at the centre?
items.e: The slices go all the way around the centre: 360°. 360° ÷ 8 = 45°. (22.5° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Noah leans a ladder against a wall. The wall is upright and the ground is flat. The ladder makes an angle of 72° with the ground. What angle does the ladder make with the wall?
items.e: The wall, the ground and the ladder make a right-angled triangle. 180° − 90° − 72° = 18°.

items.q: A regular hexagon is split into 6 equal triangles from its centre. What is angle a?
items.e: The 6 angles at the centre go all the way around: 360° ÷ 6 = 60°. (120° is the angle inside the hexagon at a corner.)

items.q: Each angle inside a regular polygon is 150°. How many sides does the polygon have?
items.e: Each exterior angle is 180° − 150° = 30°. The exterior angles add up to 360°: 360° ÷ 30° = 12 sides.

items.q: One angle of a triangle is 60°. Another angle is twice the size of the third angle. What are the other two angles?
items.e: 180° − 60° = 120° is left. If the smaller angle is 1 part, the larger is 2 parts: 3 parts = 120°, so 1 part = 40°. The angles are 40° and 80°.

items.q: A diagonal is drawn in a rectangle. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The corner of a rectangle is a right angle. 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.q: Two straight lines cross. A triangle is drawn on one side. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The angle inside the triangle at the crossing point is vertically opposite 40°, so it is 40°. 180° − 40° − 75° = 65°.

items.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x, 2x and 2x. What is x?
The angles are on a straight line. What is the value of x?
What is the smaller angle between the hands of the clock at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 hour spaces go around 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: A pair of scissors is like two straight lines crossing at the screw. The handles are opened to an angle of 35°. What is the angle between the blades?
items.e: The angle between the blades is vertically opposite the angle between the handles, so it is equal: 35°.

items.q: Ethan turns from facing north to facing south-east, turning clockwise. How many degrees does he turn?
items.e: North to east is a right angle (90°). East to south-east is half a right angle (45°). 90° + 45° = 135°.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 5 o’clock?
items.e: Each hour space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. (210° is the larger angle, the other way round.)

items.q: This is a kite. Work out the missing angle.
items.e: The two side angles of a kite are equal. 70° + 130° = 200°, 360° − 200° = 160°, and 160° ÷ 2 = 80°.

items.q: In triangle ABC, angle A is 34° and angle B is 3 times the size of angle A. What is angle C?
The end of a roof is an isosceles triangle. The angle at the top is 110°. What angle does each sloping side make with the bottom beam?
items.e: 180° − 110° = 70° is shared by the two equal angles: 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.
